note: Sequoia National Park foothill campground in oak woodland near the Marble Fork of the Kaweah, 4 miles inside the Ash Mountain entrance on the Generals Highway. Lengths vary site to site (three sites take cars and vans only); the booking site lists each. The park advises vehicles over 22 ft, trailers included, not to continue up the Generals Highway from here to the Giant Forest; longer rigs bound for Giant Forest or Lodgepole should enter by Highway 180. A free dump station sits across the highway. --Claude
summary: recreation.gov campground + catalog, nps.gov Potwisha + conditions pages, imagery read. Open year-round, reservation-only, 4-month window (120 d, not 180), 14-night max, 6 people. $32 all year 2026/2027 (unchanged). 37 sites (stored 42), 28 take an RV 23 ft+, max 49, pull-throughs; no hookups; flush toilets + water; free dump across the highway. Not waterfront confirmed (Marble Fork ~70 m behind trees in a gorge). Pin fine.
flags: ACCESS (caveat, not a drop): rec.gov notice 'Vehicles longer than 22 feet (including trailers) are not advised between Potwisha Campground and the Giant Forest Museum' - the restriction is on the Generals Highway ABOVE the campground; Potwisha itself is reached from Three Rivers/Ash Mountain (4 mi) before that stretch. Put in the note.
RIG: nps.gov says 'tents and smaller RVs', but rec.gov's per-site catalog gives RV/Motorhome lengths to 49 ft and 28 of 37 sites take 23 ft+; the per-site lengths outrank the wording.
SITES: count 42 (note prose) -> 37 per the rec.gov catalog (numbers 08, 34, 36 absent).
BOOKING: rec.gov reservationWindow is 4 Months -> window_opens_days 120 (overrides the federal row's 180).
PHONE: stored 559-565-3341 is the park's general line (nps.gov); rec.gov gives the campground's own '(559) 565-3714' - suggest 559-565-3341 -> 559-565-3714.
WATERFRONT: not waterfront confirmed - the Marble Fork is ~70 m west of sites 16/18/20 in a rocky gorge behind continuous trees, creek-size; the Middle Fork is across the Generals Highway.
STATUS: open now (nps.gov conditions, Nov 2026); wood and charcoal fires prohibited at present. Buckeye Flat (closed 2026) and South Fork (closed until further notice) are separate campgrounds.
